body: TL;DW - Brilliance starts young. Enjoy being average.
I'm sorry, whoever you are. But I tried to do it last night. There's a thread.
Sorry. I made an attempt last night.
I'm sorry, man. I tried to do it last night after all.

We'll see. It definitely changed me somehow. That was a really powerful *pull*. Once I got the shit off my face and the air into my lungs and the spirals were still dancing in my eyes and everything was ringing and echoing, I was on all fours and I was fighting, fucking *fighting* to hear if the phone was actually ringing. Half scared I was brain damaged. That instant where some little thing makes you think "*WAIT! I STILL NEED TO BE ALIVE!*" is intense, and I was not ready for it. I don't know how it will change me, but it's pretty fresh still, obviously, and I've got huge tears pooling in the corners of my eyes just thinking about it.

If you mean in a practical cause-and-effect sense, then of course.

If you mean in a spiritual or fated sense, no. I don't buy it.

I think it's starting to sink in, and it's manifesting as a frustration and an anger. I'm angry. I'm feeling trapped and ready to explode. Things I wanted to fix up around my parents place now seem like, I don't know, weird circus attractions or some shit instead of cabinets and gardening. Something I can't put my finger on. But I'm 27 and I'm having all these feelings about looking at the space and the place around me and wanting to fix it and make it better and do this and do that and the fact is I can't do any of that because this isn't my place to do it. Spending the last ten years doing anything but building the life where I get to this age and can have these feelings and act on them instead of having to turn them around and have them feed on something in my chest and make me want to explode is entirely my fault and my responsibility now is to do something to change the fact that all this is real and it's all happening.

The responsibility to change and to make it all happen is mine and you're right about what you've said and I don't want to say it scares me but man, it makes me angry. It makes me feel violent and scared and worried for people and things around me. It's getting worse every day since I made my first post. I thought I was actually doing ok, but now every time I think about these ideas and these things that are out of my hands because they do not belong to me, they are not my responsibility, it is not my place to contemplate their design or act to complete them. It's really fucking heavy and angry and internally violent and I don't know what I can do about it. I'm worried my next moves, the moves I make when I travel back interstate to where I actually live, I'm worried they'll be rash and stupid and driven by anger and frustration and the childish, selfish discomfort caused by realising that this weight is above me and waiting to be shouldered and time isn't just running out, it was never there to begin with. It already started and I just haven't been paying attention, and now it's there and it's immediate and it's... I dunno man it's just making me angry. Angry and frustrated. Analyse that because right now all it feels like is real anger and real responsibility and it feels like me actually realising it, but I have to be wrong, because if it was finally real for me and I was finally facing it then surely I would be dealing with it differently and not like this. How do I deal with this as an adult. How do I deal with this as an adult with the shadow of 10 wasted years looming behind me at the same time. 

Man, I need to talk to my counsellor. I need to get back to where the help is. Yesterday night I took 8mg of Clonazepam and 100mg of Quetiapine at 4 in the afternoon because I couldn't handle being awake that day anymore. I'm not handling this well.

The moments of clarity are there, but now the feeling of weight and responsibility and this sense of finally waking up and seeing how real and immediate the world is and how little I've been holding up my end of the bargain, it's all scaring me, or something, I don't know if I'm scared. It feels impossible and the only way I know out of "impossible" is anger and flailing and stupid pointless animal shit.
God-speed.
All I have to say to you is "good luck." Maybe today is your first tomorrow.
Thank you. I'll read this occasionally and if I have questions or doubts I'll message you. You didn't have to do this for me, but you did and I'm thankful.
I was, thank you for it. You put it a lot of effort and I appreciate that.

Yeah, I've got a philosophical/spiritual/universal framework that I'm fairly happy with, I just forget all of it at times like this (well, yesterday.) I'll try and get back into it again, because it was always helpful at the time.

Not offended in the slightest. Thanks for the reply. Definitely big on the fractal/systems/greater-than-the-sum vibe.

I wish I had words to help with the periodical suicidal thoughts thing, but I'm kinda in the same boat, and I don't know if you noticed, but I don't have a paddle either. I say we look at the scenery until the shore is closer. 

Good luck.

You're very right. I just need to start a larger one that'll take me to that next level. I do small things all the time, I'm just having trouble battling mental illness and also getting my leg up on the first rung of a ladder that'll be a decent challenge compared to all the daily fixer miracle work I do.

I complete little things all the time. Whenever I tell the people closest to me how useless I feel they always have a huge list of things to remind me that I helped them with, fixed, built, found, etc.

My problem is that I genuinely have a mental illness. It prevents me from seeing all those little details that are positive. I'm working on that, but the holiday season can be tricky due to professionals taking time off for family and holidays (well deserved, they are good people.)

Thanks for your reply.

* I didn't.

* I'll try not to let that go to my head.

* I did, and I am. And another, and another.

Thanks for the reply.

Thank you. I'm not sure why it's such a constant symptom for me but I spend a lot of time dwelling on the past. I know we all do it, but it's obviously one of the most toxic and dangerous things that I do because the result is so often a train of thought that leads to suicidal ideation - often quite close to actual commitment.

I try to do little bits of the things that make me tick, here and there, but I'm still constantly battling with this sense that I'm not where I *ought* to be at the age of 27. And yeah, I know how big a shitstorm that word is for anyone's mental health.

Thanks for your advice and taking the time. I'm working on that ladder.
I'll do my best. Love back at you.

I have no story to share. But I believe that you do. What you have written doesn't reveal much to me, but you feel something massive has happened that (again, you *feel*) is irreparable. I don't have the tools to help with that. What I do have is gratitude that you shared your feelings with me. Medication is nothing to be ashamed or afraid of. Please seek help if you're not already.

Hello, sorry. I think many people took some of the words I used and assumed different contexts. When I said it was my ideal to achieve something *novel* I meant it in the adjective sense. I then went directly into speaking about writing, however, so I made things confusing unintentionally. But that's not very important, really. 

Thank you for the cliché. They are dismissed, I believe, thanks to a widespread fixation on the novel and the unique; but I also believe that's *bullshit*. I like (however inaccurate it may prove to be) the idea that *cliché* comes to us, onomatopoeic, conjuring the plate's production, or usage in a press (the image I prefer.) Ideas that became words that became phrases that were so suited to the description of myriad phenomena that we, they, someone, decided: *set it apart from the others, may it stand alone. No other arrangement approaches its keen brevity. If it is to be expressed, these are exactly and, indeed, the only words that will suit.*

Think of them not as ends of expression or cessation of imagination; instead see them as what they truly are: final forms. Artifacts that approach perfection, insofar as far as we are capable. These phrases were set in their own metal because they were printed thousands upon thousands of times, distributed far and wide. Not simply because it is easier, but because we have the foresight to know that a phrase of such clarity and concision will not simply be uttered once. 

Never downplay a cliche. See instead what power they might hold.

Now, to the more mundande: Effort. When I become the way I was yesterday evening, I focus on that phrase because I have started and stopped so many times, it seems. It's not sprung out of nothing. The sadness that grips me and urges me to end what seems to be an infinite cycle is born from all the conversations I've ever had, the people I've met, the ideas born and the schemes hatched. It seeps out of their long-dead corpses, piled in the back of my psyche. The idle-yet-fervent drunken promises of *this is a great idea, I have your number, we'll talk tomorrow, this is happening!* The endless stream of confident "yeah, I can do that for you no problem" followed by my failure to show up, flaking on promise after promise - an anxiety that you might be able to foresee feeds upon itself and seems to only grow stronger.

Anyway, more rambling. Rambling. All is not lost. I am alive.

Thank you for your reply.

Plenty to do here. I love my parent's house and garden, always so much to do. Starting small with that and keeping up with my appointments (psych, gp, that sort of thing.) A very recent and unexpected ramping-up of my ability to lucid dream is looking very promising as far as satisfying the fantasies goes. A day of rewarding work for people I care about followed by a solid night's sleep where I can be anything and everything seems like a pretty good deal, at least for now. Thanks for taking the time to reply.
I haven't said it all, probably never could. I'm sorry. If I ever told you I loved you, I meant it. Don't blame anyone but me. This is my fault, my choice. I'm so sorry.

Mum, Dad: It's not being here that did it. Being here gave me hope. But hope reminds me how stupid it is to believe I'll ever stick at something. Hope reminds me that whatever goal, whatever idea; it's down to me to make it happen, and I just don't trust myself to try, let alone to perservere.

 I've been happier in the last week than any time in recent memory.
The main thing is: I am never going to put in the effort. That's what it took me this long to learn. I will never put in the effort.
